maria chen: Quick follow-up to the FP8/INT8/4-bit RFC — we need to lock the runtime <-> ops interface and telemetry before the canary. short checklist below, want alignment.

jon p: Agreed. Two urgent questions: (1) request-level semantics for precision (preference vs hard), (2) what lightweight signals should trigger automatic fallback.

alina ivanova: For (1) we should expose a `precision_hint` enum: `require`, `prefer`, `allow`. If `require` fails quality checks, runtime returns 409 or routes to a fallback model. `prefer` should let runtime try lower-bit then fallback silently if regression detected.

nate: +1 to that enum. For (2) telemetry: we need per-request deltas for logprob, token-entropy shift, and a simple human-readable `degradation_score`. ops wants streamable metrics.

samir: Can we keep the runtime contract tiny? Proposal: request header `X-Precision-Hint` and optional `fallback_policy` JSON blob. Example:
```json
{"precision_hint":"prefer_fp8","fallback_policy":{"on_quality_drop":"int8","max_latency_ms":1200}}
```
This keeps control with caller but lets runtime make safe choices.

jon p: That JSON blob is fine but we should avoid arbitrary blobs in hot paths. Maybe allow either a short header (`prefer_fp8`) or a signed policy reference (policy-id) that ops resolves.

alina ivanova: Agree on signed policy-id pattern — small header for low-latency callers, policy-id for enterprise. Also add a runtime-exposed endpoint for policy metadata for debugging.

ops-bot: notice: Canary window for quantized paths scheduled 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC — ensure telemetry hooks are in place.

maria chen: On telemetry signals, minimal required set: `per_token_avg_logprob`, `prefix_shift` (first N tokens), `degradation_score` (0..1), `latency_ms`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`. Ops: do you need anything else?

nate: Add `topk_consistency` (how often top-1 changes vs baseline) and `rare_token_regressions` (count of low-frequency token mismatches). Those catch hallucination spikes.

samir: Implementation note: keep telemetry as a sampling stream (1% by default) and full for canary traffic. Don't degrade p99.

jon p: Runtime fallback semantics: when degradation_score > 0.25 (tunable), and latency within max allowed, trigger fallback to fallback_policy model. Also emit an event `precision_fallback` with reason tag.

alina ivanova: Also record root-cause hint: `attn_head_instability` or `out_of_vocab_shift` based on simple heuristics, to speed triage.

maria chen: Good. Last piece: developer ergonomics. Add a CLI: `rwdctl quant-check --policy <id> --prompt example` that runs a tiny shadow eval and reports delta metrics. Ops + eng-runtime own this.

nate: I'll sketch the runtime PR: header parsing, policy lookup, degradation scoring hook, fallback emitter. Samir can add sampling knobs in the ops side.

samir: I'll add config flags in dedicated: `quant.sample_rate`, `quant.max_fallback_latency_ms`, and `quant.degradation_threshold`.

jon p: One more: versioning. Policy-id must embed semantic version and model-compat tag. No runtime will accept policy with unknown model-compat.

maria chen: Thanks — seems like strong alignment. I'll draft the follow-up RFC + decision log with the enum, header/policy-id pattern, minimal telemetry set, fallback semantics, and the `rwdctl` command. Targeting PR by EOD. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: Please add instrumentation tickets to the canary epic before EOD.
